standard_prerequisites.name: Cone and distinguished triangle in a dg module category
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cone of a morphism of dg modules, with its canonical triangle, and the fact that an additive functor compatible with cones respects distinguished triangles.
standard_prerequisites.use: The identification of the Hom complex into a cone with the cone of the Hom complexes is the exactness argument (source lines 5454-5466).

standard_prerequisites.name: Right derived functor and essential constancy
standard_prerequisites.statement: A right derived functor on a triangulated category is computed by an essentially constant diagram indexed by the quasi-isomorphisms out of a representative, when it is everywhere defined.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the mechanism that produces the derived functor and the reduction to the abelian-group level (source lines 5467-5474).

standard_prerequisites.name: Associated functor on complexes
standard_prerequisites.statement: The author's construction gives a functor from the homotopy category of complexes of A-modules to the homotopy category of dg E-modules (the author's lemma lemma-construction, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at the start of the proof as the functor whose exactness is established (source line 5452).

core_obligations: Take the associated functor on complexes and claim exactness: invoke the retained lemma lemma-construction to obtain the functor from K(A) to K(Mod_{(E,d)}) and reduce the exactness claim to compatibility with cones (source lines 5450-5453).

Identify the Hom complex into a cone: for a map of complexes f : A -> B, show by a direct computation that the Hom complex from K into the cone of f is the cone of the induced map between the Hom complexes from K into A and into B, in the dg E-module category; conclude that the functor is compatible with cones and hence with distinguished triangles (source lines 5454-5466).

Pass to the derived category: for an object X of K(A), use the everywhere-definedness of the derived functor to conclude that the quasi-isomorphism-indexed diagram is essentially constant in derived abelian groups, and transfer that to the derived category of dg E-modules because the forgetful functor is compatible with cohomology (source lines 5467-5474).

proof_roadmap.step: Invoke lemma-construction and reduce the claim to compatibility with cones.
Compute the Hom complex into a cone as the cone of the induced map, giving exactness.
Use essential constancy of the quasi-isomorphism diagram and compatibility of the forgetful functor with cohomology to build the derived functor.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-existence-of-derived at source lines 5436-5447: if the right derived functor of Hom(K, -) from the homotopy category to derived abelian groups is everywhere defined on the derived category, then there is a canonical exact functor of triangulated categories from the derived category to the derived category of dg E-modules, reducing to the usual one on the level of complexes of abelian groups. The proof at source lines 5449-5475 has to do two separate things. It first takes the associated functor on complexes supplied by the author's construction and proves it is exact by identifying the Hom complex out of K into the cone of a map f with the cone of the induced map of Hom complexes, which is a genuine computation and is what makes the functor compatible with distinguished triangles. It then has to pass to the derived category: using that the derived functor is everywhere defined, it argues that the quasi-isomorphism-indexed family defining it is essentially constant in derived abelian groups, and transfers that constancy to the derived category of dg E-modules using that the forgetful functor is compatible with taking cohomology. The statement records only the conclusion. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
